claim: Multi-pulse adaptive strategy combining different pulse durations based on both target range and clutter characteristics optimizes detection while minimizing false alarms
mechanism: The radar system employs a sequence of pulses with different durations in each dwell, with each pulse optimized for specific conditions. A short pulse maintains resolution for near targets, a medium pulse balances resolution and energy for mid-range targets, and a long pulse maximizes energy for distant targets while being weighted based on local clutter conditions.
evidence: Some bioacoustic systems use multiple call types in sequence
Multi-pulse radar techniques exist but are not commonly adapted to clutter suppression
Frequency diversity approaches have shown promise in radar applications
assumptions: Multiple pulse types can be generated and processed within real-time constraints
Clutter characteristics vary sufficiently across ranges to justify multiple pulse types
Target returns can be correctly associated with the appropriate pulse type
Processing hardware can handle the increased computational load
expected_failure_modes: Increased pulse sequence reduces dwell time on targets
Processing multiple pulse types exceeds FPGA capabilities
Pulse interactions create new interference patterns
novelty_rationale: Combines range-based and clutter-based adaptation strategies in a multi-pulse approach, analogous to how some bioacoustic systems use multiple signal types in sequence
testability: Can be implemented by modifying the radar to generate a sequence of differently duration pulses in each dwell and analyzing the results separately
falsifier: If the multi-pulse approach shows no improvement in false alarm rate or detection probability compared to single adaptive pulse approaches, or if the processing requirements exceed real-time capabilities
